transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-08-14
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Kim (Redwood SE), Lena Torres (Emergent CISO), Raj Mehta (Emergent Head of Cloud), Sophie Lane (Emergent Compliance), Eli Navarro (Emergent DevOps)

Summary:
Quick security posture discovery focused on hosted vs dedicated vs private deployments. Customer cares about SOC2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, and data retention. Agreed to follow-ups: send attestations, share private deployment diagram, schedule infra benchmark.

Topics:
- Compliance attestations (SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001)
- Authentication & SSO (SAML, SCIM provisioning)
- Encryption at rest / KMS - customer-managed keys
- RBAC and tenant isolation for Dedicated/Private
- Audit logs and retention/exportability
- Data residency & retention policies
- Proof-of-concept benchmarks and timeline

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, that's Jordan our solutions engineer. Quick intros?
[00:08] Lena: Hi I'm Lena, CISO at Emergent. We're evaluating options for hosting LLM features — low latency for clinician workflows but we also have strict PHI rules.
[00:17] Raj: Raj here, we run most infra in us-central and europe-west, curious about VPC options and network controls.
[00:24] Sophie: Sophie, compliance. Need to understand attestations and data retention controls.
[00:30] Jordan: Great, we'll run through our security posture and then dig deeper into any areas you want. Sorry in advance if transcription glitches, my mic is a little loud.
[00:39] Maya: The big picture: Redwood offers Hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private deployments. The security guarantees differ — Hosted is multi-tenant with strong controls and SOC2 Type II, Dedicated gives isolated GPU pools and network controls, Private is customer-managed in VPC or on-prem.
[00:58] Lena: Can you confirm you have SOC2 Type II and ISO? It's a gating requirement for us.
[01:04] Maya: Yes we have SOC2 Type II current through 2026 and ISO 27001 attestation — I'll send the certs after the call.
[01:12] Sophie: Is the SOC scope inclusive of hosting and key management? We need details on scope.
[01:18] Jordan: Short answer: SOC covers our hosted control plane and production inference runtime. For KMS, we support customer-managed keys for Dedicated/Private via KMS integrations; we'll include the exact scope in the docs we send.
[01:31] Raj: On KMS, does Redwood support AWS KMS and GCP KMS for Private? We need CMEK for some environments.
[01:38] Jordan: Yes, we support AWS KMS and Cloud KMS via integrations for Private deployments, and Dedicated can be configured to use your KMS for encryption at rest. Hosted can offer envelope encryption with customer-managed keys via our KMS bridge — there's a short lead time for onboarding.
[01:53] Lena: How about SSO — SAML, SCIM for provisioning? Our SSO team requires IdP metadata and SCIM.
[01:59] Maya: We support SAML 2.0, OIDC integration, and SCIM for user provisioning. For Dedicated and Private you get full SSO setup and RBAC controls; for Hosted there's tenant-level RBAC with SCIM provisioning as well.
[02:12] Sophie: Is there role separation for auditors vs devs? We need read-only auditor access to logs.
[02:18] Jordan: Yes RBAC supports role templates, and we can provision read-only auditor roles. For Private you'll manage roles through your IdP, and we can map to Redwood roles.
[02:29] Eli: For audit logs, what granularity? We need API-level logs, admin changes, and model version rollouts captured. Also exportability to our SIEM.
[02:38] Jordan: We emit admin audit logs, API request/response metadata (note full request bodies for PHI are handled per retention rules), and deployment events. Logs can be pushed to your cloud logging (CloudWatch/Stackdriver) or exported via S3 delivery for Dedicated/Private. Hosted customers can request log forwarding with an EDL.
[02:57] Lena: About data retention — we have a 7-year retention for some records but also need ability to delete data on request and enforce retention windows. How does Redwood handle request-level retention and deletion?
[03:07] Maya: For Hosted we have configurable retention windows and can purge data on request; for Dedicated/Private you control retention entirely. We also support automated redaction at ingest for certain PII types, but we recommend private deployments for high-PHI workloads.
[03:23] Sophie: Need details on deletion guarantees and proof for audits.
[03:27] Jordan: We'll include our deletion playbook and retention controls in the packet — includes logs showing deletion operations and typical RTO for compliance requests.
[03:36] Raj: Network controls — can we do VPC peering, private endpoints, and egress control? We need no public internet egress for model traffic.
[03:44] Jordan: Private supports VPC peering and on-prem. Dedicated supports private endpoints and egress controls via NAT configuration. Hosted has private connectivity options via customer VPN/PrivateLink in select regions. We'll add architecture diagrams where each option is shown.
[03:59] Lena: What about model artifacts and storage? Are model weights encrypted at rest? Who has access?
[04:06] Maya: Model artifacts are encrypted at rest; access is limited to the runtime service account. For Private deployments the artifacts live in your storage and you control access. For Hosted we use customer-specific namespaces and strict IAM.
[04:18] Eli: Performance question — if we do Dedicated or Private, what does the rollout look like for canary and fallback? We need predictable latency.
[04:25] Jordan: We support rollout policies, canary, A/B, and automatic fallback to smaller models. We'll coordinate a benchmark run with your test prompts to establish SLOs.
[04:35] Lena: Any third-party pen tests or vulnerability scanning?
[04:38] Maya: We run regular internal scans and annual external pen tests; summary reports available under NDA. Also we have a bug-bounty program.
[04:47] Sophie: Is there an on-prem air-gapped option? Our legal team asked about it for PHI workloads.
[04:52] Jordan: Yes we offer on-prem packages for air-gapped deployments — it's a larger engagement but supported. We'll add a short note on scope and timeline for air-gapped installs.
[05:02] Raj: Quick question on SLA — uptime and latency SLAs for Dedicated?
[05:06] Maya: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime targets and latency SLOs tailored to the reserved capacity. We'll include our SLA doc.
[05:13] Lena: Ok would like to see SOC2, ISO, pen-test summary, deletion playbook, and private deployment diagram. Also need to lock in dates — we may have an audit in Q4.
[05:24] Maya: Understood. We'll get the packet together and propose the infra deep dive w/c 8/24.
[05:29] Sophie: One more — legal will ask about data processor agreement and standard DPAs.
[05:33] Maya: We'll include our DPA and standard security addendum.
[05:36] Jordan: I'll own the architecture diagram and the benchmark plan.
[05:39] Eli: I'll prep sample prompts and environment details.
[05:42] Maya: Great, any other blockers?
[05:45] Lena: No blockers, just need the docs for our risk review.
[05:49] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule.
[05:52] Raj: Thanks, bye.
